name: external_crossflow_cylinder
title: External forced convection: crossflow over a single cylinder (function library)
summary: Eight EES FUNCTIONs returning the average Nusselt number of a single circular cylinder in crossflow: Zukauskas (piecewise in Re, with the wall-Prandtl correction), Churchill-Bernstein, Sanitjai-Goldstein, Fand, McAdams, Whitaker and the two forms of Perkins-Leppert (1962 and 1964), the last three with the viscosity-ratio correction. Re, Pr, Prw and the viscosities are arguments, so the calling model passes them; the surface heat-transfer coefficient follows from h = Nu*k/D and is left to the caller.

authors: S. W. Churchill and M. Bernstein (Churchill-Bernstein correlation)
S. Sanitjai and R. J. Goldstein (Sanitjai-Goldstein correlation)
H. C. Perkins Jr. and G. Leppert (Perkins-Leppert 1962 and 1964 correlations)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/conv_external.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block (Zukauskas 1972 and Churchill & Bernstein 1977 as in Bergman et al. 6E; Sanitjai & Goldstein 2004; Fand 1965; McAdams, Heat Transmission, 3E, 1985; Whitaker 1972; Perkins & Leppert 1962 and 1964). The optional Prw argument of Nu_cylinder_Zukauskas and the optional mu/muw arguments of Nu_cylinder_Whitaker, Nu_cylinder_Perkins_Leppert_1962 and Nu_cylinder_Perkins_Leppert_1964 became mandatory (EES has no optional argument; pass Prw = Pr or mu = muw for the uncorrected form). Two discrepancies between the ht docstring and its code are resolved in favour of the code and noted in the function comments (Whitaker uses Pr^0.3, Sanitjai-Goldstein carries the power -5 of its first exponential term inside the exponential). The HT-008 inventory note saying that Nu_cylinder_Whitaker takes a D^2/(L D) geometry parameter does not apply to ht 1.2.0 (signature: Re, Pr, mu, muw). Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: case A: the 11 values published by ht 1.2.0 - the eight doctests of ht/conv_external.py (one per correlation) and the three viscosity-ratio values of ht/tests/test_conv_external.py - plus the uncorrected Zukauskas form; case B: values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv; 24 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 36 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 2 (the Zukauskas inputs of the uniform case B, which the Python reference lists twice), only in CoolSolve: 0. Largest relative deviation 1.9e-13 (Nu_cylinder_Churchill_Bernstein_B), i.e. round-off in the double-precision evaluation only.
